_comment: Fictitious clinical catalog. All codes are invented: DXCODE source codes use letter prefixes Q-Z, which no real diagnosis classification issues, and the 3-character prefix groups a genuine disease family, so prefix-based recall returns genuine clinical siblings. Prevalence targets are calibrated to published US adult epidemiology so a literature-comparison step agrees by construction.  seasonality names a profile in calendar.json; without it every onset is drawn uniformly over the observation window and monthly counts come out flat, which no real disease does. cause_of_death_weight is the relative propensity that a decedent carrying this condition died *of* it, used to fill death.cause_concept_id instead of the constant 0 it held before. monotonic_age asserts that recorded prevalence must rise with age; the validation suite fails the build if it does not, which is how the 80+ hypertension dip was caught. valid_from/valid_to bound when the disease and its codes could exist at all. assigned_by marks a condition the population sampler must skip because a dedicated episode generator owns it - the maternal and perinatal conditions are assigned by the pregnancy model, not by prevalence sampling.
_cause_of_death_comment: cause_of_death_weight values are FITTED relative propensities, not clinical quantities, and they span four orders of magnitude because the competition is between conditions that co-occur constantly. A decedent's underlying cause is drawn from {natural} plus every condition they carried whose onset preceded death, with probability proportional to these weights. They were fitted by iterative proportional scaling over a 60,000-patient simulation until the realised mix matched a target distribution: heart disease 18.7%, stroke 5%, COPD 5.5%, dementia 4.5%, cancer 6.9%, diabetes 3%, sepsis/pneumonia/COVID 8%, renal and hepatic 3.9%, accidental 6%. Two consequences are deliberate and should not be read as defects. First, hypertension sits at 0.10 while CAD sits at 116: two thirds of decedents carry hypertension, so without a near-zero weight it becomes the leading cause in the file - it was recorded on 13% of deaths before this was fitted, roughly four times its real share. Second, cancer reaches only about 7% of deaths against the true US figure of 18%, because the catalog carries four cancer sites and those four are only about 45% of US cancer mortality; the shortfall is coverage, not calibration, and is recorded in KNOWN_QUIRKS.md.
